invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).

Every save control a page offers makes exactly the same checks on that page's answers, with no page an exception: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered still shown, and the controls differ only in where they go once every answer passes (ruling:sam-2026-10-26).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Germinal Commodity details asks total gross weight, number of packages and temperature, and the backend stores and publishes them with interim typeCodes
increments.detail: The germinal set's copy of Commodity details asks, for each chosen species, an optional 'Total gross weight' in kilograms followed by a 'Number of packages', and always asks one optional 'Temperature' for the consignment after all the commodity blocks. A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row listing all its chosen species, and its block is headed by the commodity's name and code. The animals backend holds the gross weight as a decimal on each species line and the temperature on every line of the notification, and shows both back; neither is published, because the profile the service publishes against carries no field for them. The number of packages is the line's quantity when the notification is published. While the catalogue still holds combined embryos-and-ova lines, each germinal trade line carries an interim type code: SEMEN for a semen line and EMBRYO for a combined line, so a combined line submitted in that time records ova as embryos. The germinal set always asks the consignment's temperature. The current published profile has no field for it, so the animals backend is its only home: it stores the answer and shows it back, and the published payload carries none of it. A germinal products notification is published on the same events and payload as a live-animals one, carrying only what the gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0 profile already defines; the sections the germinal set never asks (unweaned animals, the CPH number, per-animal permanent addresses) are left out, as the mapper leaves out any unanswered section. No profile version, shared data shape or gateway mapping changes for the germinal set's own details: the profile update for them is another team's work, outside this backlog. Once germinal trade lines carry their own type codes, every live-animal trade line says what it is too.
acceptanceCriteria: Each germinal species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before 'Number of packages'; left blank it shows no error and saves. increments.title: With JavaScript, transit countries are added as they are picked and removed in place, announced as 'Added' and 'Removed'
increments.detail: A trader says which countries the consignment travels through by picking each one from a country search. With JavaScript the picked country joins the list of added countries straight away, Remove takes one off without reloading the page, and a screen reader hears 'Added <country>' and 'Removed <country>'. Without JavaScript the page keeps working exactly as it does today, so this enhancement waits: design must say whether adding on pick, removing without a page load and the 'Added'/'Removed' wording are strongly needed and which tested library should provide them. It is built as design says, or dropped if design drops it. However it is built, the saved answer stays a list of country codes and every check on the transit list stays.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, choosing a country from the transit country search adds a row for it to the added-countries table straight away, with no page load, and clears the search box ready for the next country (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-093, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-029; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-055)

increments.title: Germinal identification asks once per species for donor, dates and identification number, and the backend stores them unpublished
increments.detail: Germinal products are identified once per species, whatever the number of packages. The germinal set's copy of Identification details shows each chosen species one editable form, headed by the species name with no count, prefilled with what was saved, with no panel button and no table of saved entries. The form asks for a donor name or identification, a collection date, a production date and an identification number or mark, in that order, for every germinal commodity the set offers. The panel keeps the species heading and the link back to Commodity details, and the page's Selected commodities summary counts packages rather than animals. Valid germinal Commodity details lead here. The germinal products set's copy of the identification page summarises the consignment's selected commodities, as the live-animals page does, but a germinal consignment is counted in packages. Its quantity column is headed 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved count, where the live-animals page keeps 'Number of animals'. The germinal set collects a donor name or ID, a collection date, a production date and an identification mark for each germinal species. The current published profile has no field for any of them, so the animals backend is their only home: it stores them, the service shows them back, and the published payload carries none of them. Each date is held as a date-only YYYY-MM-DD value. Where they sit on the record, on the per-item identifier entries of each line as the record holds animal identifiers, or on the species line, is decided in the build from the real model rather than from the prototype's shape.

increments.title: A permanent address page for cats, dogs and ferrets, with one card per animal and a same-as-destination choice
increments.detail: Each pet's permanent address is asked on its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, instead of inside the animal identification form. Cats, dogs and ferrets need one. Other live mammals that share commodity code 01061900 do not. The page has a card for each animal that needs one, showing the identifiers already given, and asks for each whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, revealing the address fields only when a new address is chosen. Each animal's choice and address are stored with the notification, every field in its own place, and a trader can save what they know and come back.

increments.title: Choosing Transporter when adding to the address book hands over to adding a transporter
increments.detail: A trader who keeps transporters alongside their addresses needs to add one from the same place they add an address. 'Choose an address type' therefore offers 'Transporter' as well, and choosing it leaves the address form behind and opens the add-a-transporter pages, which start by asking what kind of transporter it is. Nobody has yet decided whether the service manages transporters at all, or whether the address book or something else does, so this waits: the option would otherwise lead nowhere. A trader who starts adding a transporter from the address book goes through the same add-a-transporter pages, but they lead back to the address book rather than into a notification: the Back link returns to the address book's add page, the cancel button offers a return to the address book, and a save puts the new transporter at the top of the address book's transporter list, held as the organisation's. Blocked: the address book's transporter rows wait on transporter management being settled. Once it is decided that the address book manages transporters, the address types a trader chooses from when adding an address include 'Transporter', so a transporter can be added to the book alongside the other parties. It is blocked with the rest of transporter management: offering the type with nowhere to add a transporter leads nowhere.

Data model settled 6 November by ruling:ian-2026-11-06 decisions 4 and 5, so this row's two open questions are closed. A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model: AddressRequest requires at least one role (@NotEmpty) and refuses a type outright (@Null, "type is not a supported field"), and a transporter carries an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status that no address has. It reuses the service's organisation scoping, soft-delete and the Standard Address Block field validation where the fields match. Transporters have no roles — no seventh AddressRole and no fourth RoleGroup — and store the private-or-commercial type instead, which decides the form, the field list and the country rule and so cannot be derived. increments.title: Same-as shortcuts on the roles and addresses page
increments.detail: Lets a trader fill the consignor from the place of origin, and the importer and the place of destination from the consignee, with one button press on the live-animals roles and addresses page. The consignor is often the farm of origin and the importer is usually the consignee, so today the trader picks the same address twice. The button copies the source party's record onto the notification as an independent copy, so a later change to the source does not ripple through.

increments.title: Picker 'View' link to the INS address book and back, and the picker's address lines and width
increments.detail: Each live animals party picker row offers a link to that saved address's own record in the Import Notification Service address book, carrying the picker it was followed from as a return parameter, so a trader who sees a wrong saved address can correct or delete the record and come straight back to the picker they left. Where a row keeps an in-place details disclosure, it stops repeating the name, address lines and country the row's own columns already show. The address book is the only place an address is written, so the record and its edit stay there; its record page already honours a return to the animals journey. High-risk plants pickers are not wired to the address book and are left alone. Replaces each live-animals picker row's in-place details expander with a 'View' link that opens the address in the INS address book, carrying that picker as its return, so a trader can read, correct or delete the record and come back to the picker they left. The INS frontend stays the one place an address is shown in full and the address book's only writer. On the animals and the high-risk plants pickers each address line shows on its own line, which reads more easily in a narrow column. The high-risk plants pickers are not wired to the INS address book, so they keep their in-place details disclosure.
acceptanceCriteria: Each live animals party picker row offers a link to that saved address's own record in the address book, carrying the picker it was followed from as a return parameter for the same notification. (document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-037, p7-042; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-064)

On the compose stack, following that link opens the address's own record page, with its Edit and Delete controls; its Back link, and the return after saving an edit, cancelling or deleting, bring the trader back to the same party picker of the same notification, with that notification's selection intact. increments.title: The county parish holding number page: who is asked, its help and hint, a blank save, and where it goes
increments.detail: A county parish holding (CPH) number is asked for every live animal kept on a holding. In the live-animals set the question applies to cattle, pigs, sheep, goats and poultry, built now over the commodities today's catalogue holds, so the same rule takes in the rest once the reference catalogue holds them with no further change. The page cannot be opened for a consignment it does not apply to. Its help gains a second place to find the number, the hint loses its punctuation, the boxes stop browsers offering saved values, and a trader can save the page blank and move on, with the gap held at submission instead. The page is a step of the consignment addresses section: opened from that page and always returning to it. The plants frontend asks for no county parish holding number and is not changed. Every changed English string gets its Welsh machine draft in the same change.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment holding cattle (0102), pigs (0103), sheep (010410), goats (010420) or poultry, whether day-old chicks, adult birds or hatching eggs, has a 'County parish holding (CPH) number' section on its consignment addresses page; a consignment holding only horses or 01061900 pets has none, and opening the county parish holding number page for it sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (confluence:6497338582 p2-099, p2-107 to p2-126; prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001, p9-002; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-025, p1-057)

The county parish holding help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' a link to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-009; trace:animals-fit p13-018; trace:e2e p6-084)

The county parish holding question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789' and describes the whole group of three boxes (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-010; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-119; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-040; trace:animals-fit p13-007)
Each of the three boxes turns browser autocomplete off and carries the pattern [0-9]* alongside the numeric input mode (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012; trace:animals-fit p13-014)

Saving the county parish holding number page with all three boxes empty leaves the notification with no county parish holding number, returns the trader to the consignment addresses page, leaves that page's county parish holding section reading as incomplete, and the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-014, p9-015, p9-004, p8-135; confluence:6497338582 p2-099; ruling:sam-2026-10-26 p1-024)

The county parish holding number page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page however the page was reached (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-117; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-043; trace:e2e p6-078)

'Save and continue' on the county parish holding number page returns to the consignment addresses page, whether the page was opened from that page, from the overview or from review (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-018; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-043; trace:e2e p6-074)

With the Welsh language chosen, the changed help paragraph and hint show in Welsh, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:frontend p10-050, p10-051, p10-052, p10-053)

increments.title: With JavaScript, the county parish holding boxes keep out non-digits and one paste fills all three, if design keeps it
increments.detail: Traders often copy the whole county parish holding number from an APHA document. The prototype's script drops anything that is not a digit as it is typed and spreads a pasted number across the boxes. This waits on design: the page already works without JavaScript, with the server's checks, and this script is built as design answers or dropped if design drops it.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, typing a letter, space or slash into a county parish holding box leaves the box as it was, and the script alone stops County, Parish and Holding at 2, 3 and 4 digits. Without JavaScript the boxes take any length, and a whole number typed in County is split on save. (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-011, p9-012)
With JavaScript, pasting '123456789' or '12/345/6789' into County fills County with 12, Parish with 345 and Holding with 6789 (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012-m3)
With JavaScript, pasting '3456789' into Parish fills Parish with 345 and Holding with 6789, leaving County as it was (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012-m3)
Filling a box leaves the keyboard focus in that box (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012)
openQuestions: Design question 7 is answered for the boxes (Sam, 20 Oct): three labelled boxes as drawn, no cursor jump, the whole number kept when typed or pasted in one go, already built without JavaScript. Still for design: whether the JavaScript digit filter and paste spreading are wanted on top. Built as design says, or dropped if design drops it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-044, p1-046, p1-048, p1-071, p1-072; c-288).
notes: Carried over from the existing row inc-093, still blocked: req-711 and req-712 both carry blockedBy design question 7 (c-288). The criteria stay as what the row builds if design keeps the prototype's behaviour; rewrite them to design's answer when it comes. Its theme is waiting-on-design.

It is the first client script on this page and needs its own bundle entry and its own with- and without-JavaScript proof. increments.title: The Overview for a germinal products notification, with Commodity details Complete on valid packages
increments.detail: The overview's task status tells a germinal trader what is left to do. The 9 October ruling splits the Commodity details completeness rule per set: on the germinal products set the task is Complete once every chosen species has a valid number of packages and any total gross weight entered is valid. The germinal data fields make total gross weight and temperature optional, so neither holds the task back. This is the Commodity details completeness half of the row; the germinal overview's own cards and regions are the notification-hub area's draft for it. Each germinal products notification needs an overview of its own in the germinal products set, showing the live-animals overview's content with the germinal differences. Germinal products are counted by packages and weight, not by animals, so the commodities block shows a packages card and a kilograms card instead of the animals card, and the kilograms card totals the gross weight entered for the consignment. Screen-reader users get the same named regions as on the live-animals overview, with the weight card named for the gross weight the set holds. The live-animals overview is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: On a germinal-products notification, the overview's Commodity details task shows Complete when every chosen species has a whole number of packages from 1 to 1,000, with total gross weight and temperature left blank. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-024, prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-021, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-023; c-232; c-234)

On a germinal-products notification, the overview's Commodity details task does not show Complete while any chosen species has no number of packages, or has a total gross weight entered that is not valid, such as 0. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-053)

On a germinal products notification's overview, 'Your commodities' shows exactly two cards: 'Packages/boxes' and 'Kilograms' (prototype:dr2-1-source p12-013; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-022, p1-023)
The 'Kilograms' card reads '0' before any gross weight is entered, and whenever the total is not a positive number (prototype:dr2-1-source p12-016)

The 'Kilograms' card totals the gross weight in kilograms entered for the consignment, showing a whole-number total as entered, for example '12' for 5 and 7, and any other total rounded to 3 decimal places, for example '2.5' for 1.25 and 1.25 (prototype:dr2-1-source p12-016; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-022)

On a germinal products notification's overview the 'Packages/boxes' card is a region named 'Packages summary' and the 'Kilograms' card a region named 'Gross weight summary' (prototype:dr2-1-source p12-013; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p11-013-m1; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-022)

On a germinal products notification's overview the 'Your commodities' block, the task list and each numbered section are regions named by their own heading (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p11-013-m1; prototype:dr2-1-source p12-013)
A live animals notification's overview shows the 'Animals' and 'Packages/boxes' cards and exactly those two cards (trace:animals-fit p4-008)

increments.title: The germinal products set's own review: germinal answers in their species blocks, its unfinished-species messages, and its shorter Addresses card
increments.detail: A trader reviewing a germinal products notification needs to read back what the germinal pages asked for: a total gross weight in kilograms that may be a decimal, a number of packages, a storage temperature and the germinal identification details, including the details that are only kept in this service. The germinal set has its own copy of the review, so the live animals review keeps the rows it shows today. The germinal set never asks for additional details, a county parish holding number or a permanent address, so its review shows no row for them and asks nothing of them before submit. Where a selected species is short of what submit needs, the review names that species and links to its block, whether one species or several are selected.

increments.title: Amend goes through a confirmation page, then opens the amend review, in animals and plants
increments.detail: A trader who amends a submitted notification is asked to confirm first, on a page of its own, and then lands straight on that notification's review page, where every answer and its Change link sit together. Today Amend on a notification's card starts the amendment at once and lands on the overview hub, one step short of the review; the plants journey does the same, and a notification's view page offers no way to amend at all. After this change one confirmation page stands in front of every way into an amendment: 'Amend this notification' on the view page and Amend on the card both open it, confirming is a form post that starts the amendment and lands on the review, and backing out leaves the notification submitted and untouched. An amendment that cannot start, because the reference is unknown or the notification is not submitted, changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list. The plants journey gets the same page and lands on its own review page. The performance suite's amendment journey follows the new landing.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification's view page, and Amend on its card in the set's notification list, open a page whose title and level-1 heading are 'Amend notification' and which asks 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?', and the notification still shows as submitted until the trader confirms (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-046, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-047, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-051; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-107, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-108; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-181; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-078)

'Yes, continue' on the amend confirmation page is a button that submits the page's form and starts the amendment, and the trader lands on that notification's review page showing it is being amended (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-048, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-081; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-110, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-124; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-081)

'No, go back' on the amend confirmation page is a link-styled control that returns to the notification's view page with the notification still submitted and nothing changed, and the page's Back link goes to the view page too (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-048; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-110; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-079)

With JavaScript turned off, choosing Amend on the view page or on the card opens the amend confirmation page, and its 'Yes, continue' still starts the amendment (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-075, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-076)

Opening or posting a notification's amend address when its reference is unknown, or when the notification is a draft, a completed one, or one already being amended, changes nothing and returns the trader, with no message, to the set's own notification list (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-075; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-129; repo:backend repo-backend-p2-092, repo-backend-p2-093; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-101, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-102)

In the high-risk plants frontend, Amend on a submitted plants notification's card and on its view page open the same confirmation page, with the same title, heading, question, 'Yes, continue' and 'No, go back'; 'Yes, continue' lands on plants' own review page for that notification, and a refused amend returns to plants' own notification list with no message (repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p3-115; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-057)

On the workspace stack the performance suite's amendment journey passes with Amend landing on the notification's amend review: its amendment-started check expects the review page, it still edits the origin page, and both its endings still pass, either cancelling at the cancel-amendment page to land on the view page whose address carries ?cancelled=1, or resubmitting through the review and the declaration (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p1-071, repo-perftests-p1-072, repo-perftests-p1-074; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-002)

With the service in Welsh, the amend confirmation page's title, heading, question and controls show Welsh text, in animals and in plants (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-089; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p3-114)
notes: Pass 2 combines the confirmation page (req-1391, req-1392), where confirming lands (req-1394), the guard (req-1487) and the performance-suite check (req-1877): one route, one page, one review and one ladder. c-190 and c-310 settle that the confirmation is a page carrying the pop-up's wording and that the card's Amend goes through it; c-189 that confirming is a form post; c-191 and c-225 that the landing is the review and the k6 check moves with it; c-198 that a refused amend goes to the set's own list. The dialog half of req-1391 and req-1392 is req-1393's, in the blocked pop-up row. The view page's 'Amend this notification' comes from inc-112 on the overview-and-review branch, which this row needs landed; the card's Amend lives in each frontend's dashboard feature, which the animals-dashboard theme also changes. Welsh for the delete and cancel-amendment strings is req-1480, carried by the delete page row. Rewritten this re-distil only to take the release name, the conflict ids and the quoted pop-up absence out of the title, detail and criteria; the substance is unchanged.

increments.title: The cancel-amendment page is one question and two controls, and returns to the submitted notification with no banner, in animals and plants
increments.detail: Cancelling an amendment is confirmed on a short page: a question as its heading, no explanation, a button to confirm and a plain link back. Today the page asks 'Cancel this amendment?', explains that the changes will be discarded, offers a secondary button back to the notification, and carries the notification's status tag, reference and a Back link above the heading; the restored notification then opens with a success banner. increments.title: The INS front door's home becomes the overall notifications dashboard, with the performance suite's readiness probe following its heading
increments.detail: Today the INS front door's root page is a table of every notification with a reference search and a sort form. It becomes the service's home: a 'Dashboard' caption over the heading 'Import notification service', the 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons, then one section per notification category, each linking to that category's own notification list in its own frontend. The home's controls are built on today's home before this and stay when it lands. The k6 performance suite checks the home's heading and models its reads, so it changes in the same increment as the heading, never before: changing the suite first breaks every performance run, and changing the heading first makes the suite's readiness check fail after 300 seconds. The home's per-category summary waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed. The performance suite will not start a run until the stack is functionally ready, and it judges the front door ready by opening its home signed in and matching the main heading exactly. When the home's main heading becomes 'Import notification service', the probe has to change in the same increment: changed first it breaks every run on the main branch, and changed late every run's readiness fails after five minutes. The address book probe and the rule that the stack is ready only when every probe has passed once both stay as they are. The heading itself belongs to the front door's overall home, which is held until the front door dashboard's requirements are agreed, so this waits with it.

Opened with no category, the page lists action-needed notifications of every category; opened for live animals it lists only live-animals ones, a notification with no stored category counting as live animals; an unrecognised category lists every category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:6745-6747, 9027-9028; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:162-169; conflicts:c-296)

The page's 'Back' link goes to the live animals notification list at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend while it is showing live animals, and to the home while it is showing every category or an unrecognised one (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:12-24; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:156, 167; conflicts:c-250, c-295)

The list sits under a visually hidden h2 'Notifications needing action', preceded by 'Show 1-8 of <total> results', or 'Show 0 of 0 results' when there are none; with more than eight notifications the page shows eight at a time, and following a page link keeps the sort and the category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-89, app/routes.js:6630-6688, 9050; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:160-161)

Each listed notification is shown with the same notification card as the live animals list, carrying its status tag, its error message and the links its status gives it (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed action 15-16; document:dr1-parity-notes inc-030; conflicts:c-154)

The page's main content holds only its intro block, its search and sort form, its results line and its list; opening it with a delay-filter query parameter shows the same list as opening it without one (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:9022-9023, 9043-9045)
The service navigation's 'Dashboard' item is marked current on the page (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8876, 9063; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-076)

With the front door's stub mode on, which is never on in production, the page lists the built-in stub's notifications; otherwise it reads them from the notification read model, and the read model's log for that read carries the page request's trace id (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-062, p1-063)

If the read model cannot be loaded the page still shows its intro, shows the recoverable error message, responds with HTTP status 500 and logs the failure; with Welsh selected its copy shows in Welsh, marked as a machine draft; it has no serious or critical axe violations against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA tags (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-058, p1-079, p1-086)

increments.title: Search and sort the Action needed list
increments.detail: The Action needed page has a 'Search by' box and a 'Sort by:' select, and both are applied to the real list: the search matches a notification's number, commodity, consignee or consignor, and the sort is always applied, newest first when the page opens, with no unsorted state. The form is one GET form whose button submits the search and the sort together, so the page works with JavaScript turned off. The field and parameter names are the INS service's own. It waits with the page it searches.
acceptanceCriteria: The Action needed page has its own search form with a 'Search by' field and the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'; a search made while the page is showing only live animals returns only live-animals notifications (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-87; trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14, action 25; conflicts:c-250)

Searching for part of a listed notification's number, its commodity, its consignee's name or its consignor's name lists only the notifications that match; a search typed with surrounding spaces finds the same notifications, and a blank search lists them all (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-015; repo:tests repo-tests-p4-081; conflicts:c-155)
A search that matches nothing shows 'Show 0 of 0 results' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7644-7658)

The 'Sort by:' select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', with 'Newest first' selected when the page opens; choosing one and pressing the form's button re-orders the list to match, and changing the select on its own submits nothing, so the page works with JavaScript turned off (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; document:dr1-parity-notes inc-031; conflicts:c-155, c-157)
Page links keep the chosen sort, the search text and the category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-87; trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed action 25)
With Welsh selected, the search label, the hint, the sort label and the sort options show in Welsh, marked as machine drafts (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-086)
openQuestions: Blocked: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information, naming the Action needed drill-down's search and sort (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-059), until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. Who: whoever owns the INS dashboard's requirements (the rulings do not name them) must firm them up and agree them with Sam.
notes: Kept apart from the Action needed page row so that row stays reviewable in one sitting, and because this one changes what the read model stores (consignee and consignor) and how it searches.
The same search form, sort select and results line are reused by the blocked Inspection required row, which proves its own half of req-990, req-992 and req-994.

Rewritten against the wording rules, keeping the row's id: the old detail named the prototype as the thing to match and carried conflict ids, and the sort criterion quoted the rejected 'Select one' option. The sort criterion now states the exact three options the select offers, which proves there is no fourth.

The Live animals section gets its Action needed card, counted from the same set of notifications its page lists for the signed-in organisation, so the count is real rather than a fixed number. A notification's category is the one the animals backend stores on its record, an absent one meaning live animals. It waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: The Live animals section shows an 'Action needed' glance card reading 'Tasks requiring your attention', with a count and a 'View tasks' link that opens the Action needed page showing only live animals (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:57-62; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 34; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:43; conflicts:c-250)

The Action needed count equals the number of results the Action needed page lists for live animals for the signed-in organisation: 0 for a fresh organisation, one higher once that organisation submits a live-animals notification without its ITAHC, and the same when another organisation does (conflicts:c-148, c-149)
A notification whose record carries no category is counted in the Live animals Action needed card (conflicts:c-296)

The Live animals section's only glance cards are 'Action needed' and 'Status updates' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:57-70; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 30)

openQuestions: Blocked: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information, naming this glance card (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-060), until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled, settling how the category reaches the INS read model. req-975's germinal products half is observed in the Germinal products section row. req-978's blue Status updates and Inspection required counts are observed in the Status updated row and the plants-cards row, which build those cards.

Changes the home's template and copy in the INS dashboard feature folder, which the split-off type-question-and-templates theme owns; it builds only after that theme lands, through the home row, so those files are in shared rather than touches.

increments.title: The live animals list has 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed' tabs
increments.detail: The design separates work in flight, unfinished drafts and finished notifications, and drafts keep a home on the list. The tabs are Ministry of Justice sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list, each a link that loads the page, over the animals backend's list, which gains category and tab filters and reports the count of notifications in flight. A notification being amended stays under 'In progress'.
acceptanceCriteria: The live animals list shows three tabs, 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', as Ministry of Justice sub navigation, each a link that loads the list with that tab chosen, with or without JavaScript. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-037, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-061; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-099, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-100; conflict c-299)

increments.title: The live animals list's search and sort become one form that really searches and sorts
increments.detail: The design lays the list out in one column and puts search and sort in one form with one submit control. The afternoon ruling makes it one GET form whose icon-only submit button searches and sorts on the server, so the page works without JavaScript. Today's search matches only one exact, whole reference, so it becomes a real keyword search over the reference, commodity, consignee and consignor. The sort offers three orderings, is applied for real and breaks ties so paging is stable.
acceptanceCriteria: On the live animals list the search and sort sit in one column above the tabs inside the 'Notifications' section, with the cards in the same column below them. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-009, repo-frontend-p3-010; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-045; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p3-013; conflict c-167)

The search field is labelled 'Search by' with the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-027; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-039, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-046; repo:tests repo-tests-p4-035)

Searching lists every notification whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains the searched text, ignoring case and surrounding spaces: part of a consignee's name finds that notification, and a lower-case part of a reference finds it. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-027; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-040; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-019, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-022; repo:backend repo-backend-p3-010, repo-backend-p3-011; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010; conflict c-162)

Changing the sort select or a filter radio submits nothing by itself, and the list's only submit control is the search button. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-026, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-036; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-058; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-033 to ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-036, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-097; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-058; conflict c-299)

(prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-060; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-047; repo:backend repo-backend-p3-006, repo-backend-p3-007; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010; conflict c-161)

increments.title: The live animals list has 'Additional filters' for arrival date, date range and status
increments.detail: The design keeps the extra filters out of the way until the trader needs them. They sit inside the one GET form, built from the GOV.UK details component with GOV.UK radios and a select and a Ministry of Justice date picker at each end of the date range. The filters narrow the list for real, through the animals backend's list, and a date a filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: Inside the search form the live animals list has an 'Additional filters' disclosure, built from the GOV.UK details component, closed when the list first loads and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-030; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-049; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-101; conflict c-299)

The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small GOV.UK radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days', with those same words as its heading and as a visually hidden legend; choosing one and searching lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-031; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-050; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-055, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-060; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-001, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-003; conflict c-162)

The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two Ministry of Justice date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date', each a plain text field without JavaScript; searching lists only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates stay in the fields. (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-051, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-052; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-056, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-057, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-121; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-037 to ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-039, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-101)

With JavaScript, each date picker offers a 'Choose date' calendar that opens on the current month with weeks starting on Monday. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-057; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-101, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-102)

Searching with a start date that cannot be read as a date shows a GOV.UK error summary and the inline error 'Enter a real start date'; an end date that cannot be read shows 'Enter a real end date'; an end date before the start date shows 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'. Each time, 'Additional filters' is open, the entered text stays in the 'Start date' and 'End date' fields, and the list is shown without the date-range filter. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-102; ruling:sam-2026-10-26 ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-002, ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-003, ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-019; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p2-047; conflict c-166)

(prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-035; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-053; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-058; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-024, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-026)

(document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-002, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-025, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p2-028; repo:backend repo-backend-p3-013; conflict c-162)

notes: Pass 2 combines the disclosure, the three filter columns, the date validation and the list API's status and arrival-date filters: one section of one form over one query. Depends on the search-and-sort row, whose form the filters sit in. No custom JavaScript: the GOV.UK details component, radios and select, and the Ministry of Justice date picker the animals frontend already has; build each end of the range with the frontend's own date-field kit, which now always gives the house calendar. The 'Action required' option lists what the animals backend records as action required, which the split-off overview-and-review theme's submit row adds; until that lands it lists nothing, and 'Completed' lists nothing until the authorities' outcome feed exists (req-1082, blocked row). Both options render and narrow the list now. increments.title: The lists page 8 at a time with numbered pages, and show neither a results count nor an empty-state message
increments.detail: The design pages every list 8 at a time with numbered pagination, clamps the page so a stale address never shows an empty list, and shows no count of results and no message when a list holds nothing. Because the real search and filters apply, a page link carries them. increments.title: The live animals list's Summary shows 'Action needed' and 'Status updated' glance cards
increments.detail: What needs the trader's attention sits at the top of each category list, in two glance cards whose counts agree with the pages they link to. The afternoon ruling counts these Summary cards as the front door's summary information, so they wait until its requirements firm up.
acceptanceCriteria: The live animals list has an h2 'Summary' with two glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'Tasks requiring your attention' and a 'View tasks' link to the action-needed page for the category, and 'Status updated' with 'Changes in the past 24 hours' and a 'View updates' link to the changes page for the category. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-024; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-036 to prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-042 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-044)

The 'Action needed' card's count is the number of the category's notifications showing an 'Action required' tag, and matches the list its link opens; a notification showing a 'Delayed' tag is not counted. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-025, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-069; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p3-031; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-123; conflict c-148, c-149)
openQuestions: Blocked: the front door's dashboard requirements must firm up (Sam, 9 October). Who: Sam and the people those requirements are agreed with. Once they exist this summary information is re-distilled, and what the Summary shows, where its counts come from and which pages its links open are decided then.
notes: Nothing in the reframed list depends on this row. The counts are computed from the same set the page each link opens lists, for the signed-in organisation; the design's fixed glance numbers are overruled (c-148). Repos are the animals backend, the animals frontend and the tests suite, because the list it sits on stays in the animals frontend; re-check when it is re-distilled. The 'Status updated' count (req-1735) waits as well, in the outcomes row, because it also needs the authorities' outcomes.

increments.title: The lists' success banner is titled 'Success'
increments.detail: One success banner, titled 'Success', is shown when an action sends the trader back to a list. The message itself is the action's own. The flag on the redirect keeps triggering it, and plants' banner takes the same title in the same increment. The new wording goes in each list feature's own copy, because the shared action wording other pages use is not reworded in place.
acceptanceCriteria: After deleting a notification, the live animals list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying the delete's own message. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-020; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-062, repo-frontend-p3-063, repo-frontend-p3-136; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-101; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-093; conflict c-252)

Kept as they are, already met: the banner does not dismiss itself (req-1088), and the stale-action and problem banners (req-1089). req-1087 (a message held for the trader and shown once) is out of scope (c-252): the flag on the redirect stays. Today's copy banner is never reached, so only the delete is proven.

increments.title: The germinal products set's root renders its own copy of the reframed list
increments.detail: Each category of animal notification has its own list. It shows only germinal products notifications, and its 'Create new' starts a germinal notification in the germinal set.

increments.title: Cards show the authorities' outcomes: delayed, completed, inspection, their actions and the status-updated count
increments.detail: What the authorities decide after submission is shown on the list: a delayed notification with its reason, a completed notification in its own tab, an inspection warning, and the actions a card in those statuses offers. None of these outcomes reaches the service today, so the row waits on the authorities' case system; the status-updated count also waits on the front door's dashboard requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card whose message is the reason for the delay recorded on the notification. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-052, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-065)

A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Completed' as plain styled text rather than a tag, and is listed in the 'Completed' tab. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-061; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-068; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p3-032; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-070, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-071, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-065, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-066)

A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of its card's second row. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-069)

A card whose notification is delayed, completed, or action required with no status-driven action set of its own offers 'Copy as new' then 'View', and 'View' opens the notification's review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-047 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-049; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-048; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-054; conflict c-149, c-160)

openQuestions: Blocked: the authorities' case system must send post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record. Who: the owners of that integration must provide the outcome feed; until they do, no notification reaches these statuses and none of this can be built or observed.

Blocked as well, for the status-updated count (req-1735): the front door's dashboard requirements must firm up (Sam, 9 October). Who: Sam and the people those requirements are agreed with; the count is re-distilled with the summary information.
Whether plants' card follows the 'Completed' status is decided when this unblocks.
notes: Keeps every requirement the authorities' outcome feed blocks apart, so the list rows build now. Once unblocked, the animals backend's record takes the outcomes, statuses only ever being added, and the animals frontend's card, tabs and status filter pick them up. The 'Delayed' card's message is the recorded reason, because the design's own message there is placeholder copy. Depends on the card row, the tabs row and the glance-cards row.

increments.title: Status updates cards and the Status updated page
increments.detail: Each category gets a 'Status updates' card counting changes in the past 24 hours, opening a page that groups those notifications as Passed inspection, Needs inspection or Delayed. No service in the workspace receives inspection or delay outcomes and the INS read model holds no such state, so the cards and the page wait for the authorities' outcome feed rather than ship an always-empty page and a zero count. They also wait until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: The Live animals and Germinal products sections each show a 'Status updates' glance card reading 'Changes in the past 24 hours', its count in blue, with a 'View updates' link that opens the Status updated page showing only that category; each count equals the number of notifications that page lists for that category for the signed-in organisation (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:64-69, 73-98; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 35; conflicts:c-148, c-156, c-250)

The 'View updates' link opens a page at /changes whose browser title is 'Changes in past 24 hours - Import notification service - GOV.UK', showing the caption 'Status updated', the h1 'Changes in past 24 hours' and the description 'Notifications that have progressed, or been validated, rejected, cancelled, or replaced in the past 24 hours.' together as one intro block styled to match the home's intro (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11712-11714, app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-changes.html:31-33; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:174-179)

The page groups the signed-in organisation's notifications of the category shown whose outcome changed in the past 24 hours under h2 sections 'Passed inspection', 'Needs inspection' and 'Delayed', in that order, showing a section only when at least one notification falls in it (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:6809-6825; trace:prototype-dr2-1 status-updated action 12-14, 21-22)

The page's main content holds only its intro block and its grouped lists; its 'Back' link goes to the notification list of the category it is showing, in that category's own frontend, and to the home while it is showing every category; the service navigation's 'Dashboard' item is marked current on it (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-changes.html:9-53; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:173-188; conflicts:c-295)

Blocked: Sam's 9 October rulings also block this as INS dashboard summary information (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-062) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. Who: whoever owns the INS dashboard's requirements (the rulings do not name them) must firm them up and agree them with Sam.
notes: Cards and page kept together: each count is the page's own list, and both wait on the same two blockers. The outcome feed's own integration will need a further repo (a stub or the gateway) once it is agreed, so this row's repos are a floor.

Builds the Germinal products section's Status updates card, the half of req-979 that waits on req-977's count, so it depends on that row. req-1003 (sections for validated, rejected, cancelled and replaced) is out of scope and not built.

Rewritten against the wording rules, keeping the row's id: the old title and detail named the design release, the old detail carried conflict ids, and one criterion listed what the page does not have. That criterion now states what the page's main content holds.

increments.title: 'Information is missing' on the live animals notification list card when animal identifiers are incomplete
increments.detail: A trader who submitted a notification with its certificate but without all the animal identifiers it needs has nothing on the list to tell them so. The card now shows that information is missing, worked out from what the notification recorded at submit. A commodity line whose species asks for identifiers is incomplete when it holds fewer identified animal records than the animals it declares, and a record counts as identified once one of its identifiers is filled, so a single-species consignment with no identifier saved counts as incomplete. A trader is told on the list what still needs doing on a submitted notification that has items outstanding. The card carries the outstanding item as plain text under the reference, taken from what the record stored when the notification was submitted, with the missing certificate named first and incomplete identifiers next.

increments.title: A germinal products notification starts in its own set, with its own draft, stored category, service chrome and origin page, and each set opens only its own notifications
increments.detail: Germinal products becomes a sibling set of live animals in the animals frontend, mounted at /germinal-products with its own journey, flow, obligations, cookies, gateway and set services. Its journey pages sit at /germinal-products/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug} using the live-animals slugs, each a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the germinal differences, and its overview, check answers, declaration and confirmation pages are its own copies too. Every live-animal field that is not marked as applying to the animal journey only is carried over; the CPH number and the permanent address, which are, are not, so the set has no CPH number page and no permanent address page. This row lays the set down and proves it with its first page: starting a germinal notification creates a draft with the same kind of reference a live-animals notification gets and lands on the set's own copy of the origin page. The set's end-to-end, accessibility and security specs live in the existing animals Playwright project. The plants frontend gets no germinal set, so no germinal-only difference changes plants. Germinal products is a sibling set of live animals in the animals frontend, mounted at /germinal-products with its own journey, routes and services. A trader moving between the two sets should see one service, so every germinal page must carry the same chrome as the page it is copied from: the 'Import notification service' service navigation with the same items in the same order, the Alpha phase banner, the footer, the browser-title pattern, section captions, back links, the error summary and banners. The parts of the chrome that are scoped to a set must resolve inside the germinal set rather than falling back to live animals: the service name and the Dashboard item go to the germinal set's own root, Dashboard stays the current item everywhere inside a germinal notification, and an error on an address under the germinal set is shown in the germinal set's chrome. The shared layout already resolves these from the request's mount prefix, so this is proof that the new set picks them up, not a change to the shared layout. Live animals and germinal products are sibling sets keeping their notifications in one backend, so the stored record must say which set a notification belongs to. Each set passes its category when it creates a draft, so a germinal notification reaches the germinal products list and a live animals one the live animals list. A record with no category counts as live animals, so notifications stored before the germinal set existed stay on the live animals list without a data migration. Germinal products is a sibling set of live animals in the animals frontend and both keep their notifications in the one animals backend, so the stored record is what tells the two apart. The backend's create takes the category the set starting the notification sends and holds it at the root of the record, beside its status and reference; no later save, submit, amend, cancel-amend or copy changes it. A record with no category is read as live animals everywhere, so every notification stored before the germinal set exists stays a live-animals notification without a data migration. A notification holds commodities of its one category only, never a mix, so choosing the other type in the journey starts a new notification of that category and the abandoned draft keeps the category it was created with. The read the frontend opens a notification with hands the category back, so each set's entry guard can refuse the other category's notifications. The category stays on the record: it travels on no notification event, so the event envelope and the shared event schemas stay as they are. The field's name and values are the animals backend's to choose in its own conventions. Germinal products and live animals are sibling sets whose notifications sit in the one animals backend, so a notification can only be opened and changed in the set that owns it. Each set's entry guard reads the category recorded on the notification when its draft was created, and a notification with no recorded category is treated as live animals, so a draft stored before the germinal set existed still opens in live animals with no data migration.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a germinal products notification through the germinal set's own start creates a notification with status Draft and a reference of the form GBN-AG-<two-digit year>-<six characters>, shown in the status strip from the first page, and lands on the set's 'Origin of the import' page under /germinal-products/notifications/<journeyId>/ using the live-animals slug. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-027, -p1-048; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-055)
Every germinal products notification's reference begins GBN-AG. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-028)

The germinal origin page asks the same questions, with the same heading, hints, options and error messages, as the finished live-animals origin page, and saves its answers to the germinal notification. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-011, -p1-013, -p1-015)

The germinal set has no CPH number page and no permanent address page: opening either live-animals slug under a germinal notification shows the page not found page. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p5-076, -p5-077, -p5-078; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-015, -p3-022)

The germinal set's end-to-end, accessibility and security specs sit in the existing animals Playwright project, under tests/animals/e2e/germinal-products, tests/animals/a11y/germinal-products and tests/animals/security/germinal-products, with no new Playwright project. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-061, -p1-062, -p1-063)

The accessibility specs walk the germinal pages built so far and hold each to WCAG 2.2 AA on first load and with answers filled, under the suite's existing axe rules, and the security scan drives the germinal routes. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-062, -p1-063)
The high-risk plants frontend has no germinal set and no germinal page: its journey and its pages are unchanged by this row. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-056)

Every germinal products page shows the 'Import notification service' service navigation with the same items, in the same order, as a live animals page (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-006, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-009; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p1-006, repo-frontend-p1-010)

On every germinal products page the service name and the Dashboard navigation item link to the germinal products set's own root at /germinal-products, and following either one lands there (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-008; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-103; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p1-006, repo-frontend-p1-010; conflicts:c-314)

A draft the germinal products set creates is stored with the category germinal products, and is then listed on the germinal products list and not on the live animals list. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-006, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-029, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-030)

A draft the live-animals set creates is stored with the category live animals, and is listed on the live animals list. (repo:backend repo-backend-p3-015; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-029, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-030)

A draft the germinal products set creates is stored with the category germinal products, and a draft the live-animals set creates is stored with the category live animals, held at the root of the record beside its status and reference. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-029, -p1-030; repo:backend repo-backend-p1-001, repo-backend-p1-002, repo-backend-p2-001)

A notification stored with no category on its record is read as live animals: it opens, saves and submits in the live-animals set, with no data migration. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-029, -p1-035; repo:backend repo-backend-p1-002)

Saving, submitting, amending, cancelling an amendment and copying a notification leave its stored category as it was created with, so a copy of a germinal products notification is a germinal products notification. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-023, -p1-030; repo:backend repo-backend-p2-001)

A notification holds commodities of its one category only: choosing the other type from a live-animals draft starts a new notification of that category, and the abandoned draft keeps the category live animals. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-025, -p1-054, -p1-055, -p1-056)

The read the animals frontend opens a notification with returns the stored category, and live animals for a record that has none, so opening a germinal products notification through a live-animals page, or a live-animals notification through a germinal products page, shows the page not found page. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-031; repo:backend repo-backend-p3-019; repo:perftests repo-perftests-p1-075)

The outbox events published for a germinal products notification carry the same envelope fields as a live-animals notification's: id, aggregate id and type, sub-type, version, event type, timestamp, data, actor, status changes and metadata. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-112; repo:tests repo-tests-p3-200; c-272, c-296)

increments.title: Germinal Commodity details checks weight and packages, listing errors by question
increments.detail: The germinal set's Commodity details page lists its errors by question, all species for one question before the next, so a trader fixing several species reads one question at a time. The 9 October ruling splits that ordering rule per set, and the germinal data fields make total gross weight and temperature optional, so temperature raises no error and never appears in the summary while a blank weight saves. This is the error-ordering half of the row; the germinal weight and packages validation rules are the germinal-products area's draft for it. The germinal set's Commodity details page checks the figures it asks for: the total gross weight must be a number greater than 0, at most 1,000 kilograms and to no more than two decimal places, and the number of packages is required and must be a whole number from 1 to 1,000. Where the design gives a message it is used; the rest follow the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum. With errors on several species, every total gross weight error comes before every number of packages error, and the optional temperature never appears in the summary.

increments.title: The address book takes adds from germinal products notifications and returns to them
increments.detail: A trader adding an address from a germinal products notification's party picker crosses to the address book by the same handshake and the same add page as from live animals, and gets the same address record with the same fields and checks. The address book's journey conventions gain a registered germinal products entry, so saving or cancelling sends the trader back to the germinal set's own address-return page for that notification rather than to a live animals one. The return address is built on the server from that registered entry, never taken from the handshake, so no caller can redirect the trader elsewhere. Observable in the address book's own fit suite and in the Import Notification Service Playwright project, as the redirect the address book sends.
acceptanceCriteria: The address book's add page accepts a handshake naming the germinal products journey, as it accepts one naming live animals, and shows the same add page. (repo:frontend p9-134; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-006, p1-061)

Saving or cancelling an add begun from a germinal products notification redirects to that notification's own address-return page under /germinal-products/notifications/{notification id}, carrying the fulfilment id, the saved address id and the handshake token, and never to a live animals notification. (repo:frontend p9-134, p9-139; trace:e2e p9-014, p9-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-009, p1-011)

The redirect is built on the server from the registered germinal products entry, and a handshake that names a return address of its own is refused. (repo:frontend p9-139; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-011)

An address saved from a germinal products notification is stored as the same record, with the same fields and the same checks, as one saved from a live animals notification. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-006)

Gives the germinal products set its own roles and addresses page and its own five party pickers, copied from the live-animals addresses feature once this programme has built it, under the germinal set's own journey and routes with the live-animals slugs. The copy behaves and reads as the live-animals page and pickers do, so a trader importing germinal products records every party of the consignment within the germinal notification. Germinal products are not kept on a holding and are not pets, so the germinal set is only ever asked for the five consignment addresses: it shows no CPH number section and no permanent address section, and serves neither page. Germinal products are not kept on a holding and are not pets, so the germinal products set, copied from the live-animals addresses feature, leaves out the county parish holding number and permanent address sections and pages the live set has. increments.title: The rest of the germinal journey: arrival, transit countries, contact address, declaration and submission, certified for 'Germinal products'
increments.detail: A trader importing germinal products through another country needs to see the transit countries task on the overview, so they know it is outstanding. The task shows in the arrival section between arrival details and transport details whenever transit countries are required for the notification, is absent when they are not, and reads complete once a transit country is chosen. What makes transit countries required is decided elsewhere; this row is the overview's view of it. A trader starting a germinal products notification is never asked what the goods are certified for, because there is only one answer it can have. The draft is created with 'Germinal products' already stored, so the review shows it as settled information rather than something to answer, and the submitted notification carries it to the receiving system in the same certified-for clause a live animals notification uses. The policy page marks the certified-for field as affecting live animals only while still listing 'Germinal products' among its values; the owner's decision settles that it is held on a germinal products notification and set automatically. The germinal products set follows the same shared journey buttons and status strip as the live-animals set, taken from copies of the live-animals pages once this programme has changed them, except that the additional details, CPH number and permanent address steps never apply: 'Roles and addresses' carries no CPH number or permanent address row, and the overview carries no 'Additional details' task. The certified-for answer is set to 'Germinal products' when the draft is created, so nothing asks it and the review page shows it with no Change link. A germinal notification's status strip shows a GBN-AG reference, as a live-animals one does.

increments.title: Once commodities come from the central reference data, the germinal catalogue holds eighteen items, with embryos and ova apart and each with its own type code
increments.detail: The germinal data applies to twelve named commodities, and the published payload has separate codes for embryos and ova, so embryos and ova become separate catalogue items: eighteen in all. When the commodity list comes from the central reference data and the germinal catalogue is drawn from it, the germinal catalogue holds those eighteen items, each offering its own species, selections show as live-animal selections do, and each germinal trade line carries the code for its own product type.
acceptanceCriteria: The germinal catalogue holds 18 items, sorted by name, with their codes shown with the leading zero: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); 'Cattle, Semen' (05111000); and 'Cat, Semen', 'Dog, Semen', 'Goat, Semen', 'Horse, Semen', 'Pig, Semen', 'Rabbit/Rodent, Semen' and 'Sheep, Semen' (05119985). The catalogue offers no cat or dog embryos or ova and no poultry, fish or bee germinal product. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p5-001, -p5-031, -p5-069 to -p5-071; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-036 to -p1-038; c-229, c-230, c-germinal-products-002)

Each germinal item offers its own species: Cattle offers Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, with Bovidae as well for semen; Horse offers Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat Capra hircus; Pig Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep Ovis aries; Cat Felis catus; Dog Canis familiaris; and Rabbit/Rodent, Semen one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-138, -p2-141 to -p2-143, -p2-145 to -p2-155-m1, -p3-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-061, -p3-062, -p3-076)

Ticking Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) under Cattle, Semen shows '1 selected' with a 'Cattle, Semen (05111000):' line and a 'Bos taurus' chip, as the live-animal search does. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-063; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-009)

In the published payload each germinal trade line carries the type code SEMEN for a semen item, EMBRYO for an embryos item and OVA for an ova item, and embryos and ova are always separate trade lines. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-036 to -p1-039; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-029; c-273)
