increments.title: Party pickers filter as the trader types
increments.detail: With JavaScript, the address book list re-requests itself as the trader types in the search field or changes the Type select, after a short pause, and swaps in the table, the results line and the pagination without a full page load, so a trader narrows a long book without pressing a button. It enhances the search form that already works without JavaScript. It waits on design and the product owner answering the live-filtering question, and is built as they answer or dropped if the behaviour is dropped. With JavaScript, narrows a party picker's one-page list as the trader types, with no page reload, on both animals sets' five pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, so a trader with a long address book finds the right record without a round trip. The place of origin picker narrows by country as well, as the trader types or picks one. It waits on design: until design, with the product owner, answers the open question on live filtering, the server search behind the submitting search button is the whole search. It is built as design answers, or dropped if design drops it.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript on, typing in the address book list's search field or changing its Type select updates, after a short pause and without a full page load, the table, the results line and the pagination to the matches, with no apply button to press (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-026, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-067; c-169)

With JavaScript off, the same search field and Type select narrow the list when the search button or Enter submits the form, and the results line and pagination describe the matches (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-005; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-053, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-054; c-169)

With JavaScript on, typing in the search box of a live-animals or germinal products party picker shows, with no page reload, only the rows whose name, address lines or country contain the typed text, ignoring case, and the results count shows how many are on screen (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-074, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-075, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-076; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-067)

The high-risk plants consignor and place of destination pickers narrow the same way as the trader types (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-050, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-042; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-004)

With JavaScript on, typing in or picking a country on the place of origin picker shows, with no page reload, only the rows whose country contains the typed text or exactly matches the picked country, on both animals sets (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-055; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-055, repo-frontend-p9-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-070)
Clearing the search box shows every row of the role's list again, and the results count returns to the full total (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-102)

With JavaScript turned off, each picker's submitting search button still narrows the list on the server, as it does today (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-066; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-070)

increments.title: Waiting on design: address search's search-only layout, results as the trader types, reveal on a pick and its announcements, in the address book and the commercial transporter form
increments.detail: The design opens the add-address pages that have an address search on the search alone: the address fields, contact fields and the uses checkboxes appear once a result is picked or the trader chooses to enter the address by hand, the search box goes once a result is picked, matches list as the trader types with the typed text in bold, and screen readers hear how many results there are. All of it is JavaScript on top of a page that already works without it. It waits on two things at once: design must say whether the search keeps this search-only layout or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible, and the address lookup must become a real feature rather than a gated spike. If design keeps the layout, it is built as an enhancement, and with JavaScript off the page still shows its fields and searches on the server. A destination, consignee, importer or branch address is a UK address a trader finds by searching rather than typing out, so those add-details pages open on the address search by itself. Matches appear as the trader types, picking one hides the search and reveals the address and contact fields, an 'Enter address manually' button reveals them for a trader who cannot find the address, and screen readers hear how many results there are and which address was picked. A save with nothing picked or typed reveals the fields as well, so every error summary link reaches a field the trader can see. All of this is script on top of a page that has to work without script, so it waits: the design team has still to say whether the standard address pattern with the fields always visible will do instead, and the address lookup has still to become a real feature of the front door and its backend. If the layout is kept, it is built as an enhancement of the search that already works without script. With JavaScript, the design starts the commercial transporter form with its address fields and contact-details section hidden behind the address search and a link-style button that reveals them. Whether the fields may be hidden at all is design question 10, which design has still to answer, so this waits with the other address-search questions. Without JavaScript every field shows from the start, which is already how the form works and stays so.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, an add-address page that has an address search opens with the address fields, the contact fields and the 'What else should this address be used for?' checkboxes hidden; they are shown once the trader picks a search result or chooses to enter the address by hand, and they are shown again after a failed save when anything was picked or entered. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-089, p8-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-042-m1, p7-048; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-070)

Picking a search result hides the search box and leaves the picked name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, postcode and country filled in and still editable, with the email address and phone number for the trader to enter. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-089; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048)

Below the address search, an 'Enter address manually' link-styled button shows the address and contact fields without a result being picked. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-088; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-045)

With JavaScript, typing in the address search lists the matching addresses below it under 'Address search results', each as the lookup's one-line address with the typed text in bold. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-046)
The number of address search results is announced to screen readers through a polite live region, such as '1 result available'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-047; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-027)

Saving an add-address page that has an address search, with either save button, before anything is picked or entered shows, in order, 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number', with no country error and no error on the search itself, and shows the address and contact fields so every error summary link moves to a visible field. (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-099; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-051; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-071; ruling:sam-2026-10-26 p1-008, p1-013; conflicts:c-109)
With JavaScript off, the same page shows the address and contact fields from the start and its Search button searches on the server. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-086, p1-087)

With JavaScript on, 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' open the add-details step with only the address search; the address fields, the contact fields and the 'Address type' uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when a picked address or address line 1 already has a value (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-083, p16-096, p16-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140, p6-141)

Typing in the address search lists matching addresses below the field in a list labelled 'Address search results', each result showing the name, address and country the lookup gives, with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results, such as '1 result available' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-027, p16-029, p16-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-086, p16-086-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-143; c-178)
Below the address search an 'Enter address manually' link-styled button reveals the address and contact fields (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-085, p16-130)

Picking a search result hides the address search, reveals the address and contact fields and announces 'Selected <name>' to screen readers (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-033, p16-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-087, p16-088)

Saving the search-only layout with nothing picked or typed shows the same six field errors the manual address form shows, from 'Enter a name or organisation name' to 'Enter a phone number', with no message about the search field, and reveals the address and contact fields so each error summary link moves focus to a field the trader can see (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-092; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-142; repo:insfrontend p3-065; c-180)

increments.title: A notification needing action can be amended, copied and deleted as a submitted one can
increments.detail: A notification whose status reads 'Submitted action required' offers the trader the same actions as a submitted one, and every action must accept it, or the trader is refused on the very notification that needs their attention. Amending it opens its amendment and keeps its submitted answers aside; cancelling that amendment puts them back, and the status that follows from them; resubmitting records whatever status the outstanding items give at that moment; Copy as new copies it into a new draft; and Delete removes it and publishes its deletion. The animals sets only: the plants journey has no action-required status.
acceptanceCriteria: On the view of a notification showing 'Submitted action required', 'Amend this notification' and the amend confirmation start its amendment, as they do for a submitted one, and its submitted answers are kept aside unchanged (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-096; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-008, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-012; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-070, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-071)

Resubmitting that amendment with the outstanding document now uploaded and nothing else outstanding shows the notification as 'Submitted', and resubmitting it with items still outstanding shows it as 'Submitted action required' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-096; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-071)

'Copy as new' on a notification showing 'Submitted action required' makes a new draft carrying over the same answers a copy of a submitted one carries (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-134; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-012)

increments.title: Pressing Enter in a species panel saves that panel's own animal and reaches no other panel's buttons
increments.detail: Today one hidden 'Save and finish' submit button sits at the top of the whole form and is the default submit for every field on the page, whichever species panel the field belongs to. With a panel per species, and a 'Remove' button on every saved animal, that single default submit is the wrong owner for a field: pressing Enter in a panel's field should save that panel's current animal, as the panel's own save button does, and it should never reach a 'Remove' action or another panel's save. The trader keeps every animal they have already saved and every value they have typed, and a keyboard or screen-reader user meets no button inside a panel that is not one of the panel's own.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Enter in a field of a species panel that takes more than one animal saves that panel's current animal, as that panel's own save button does, and leaves the trader on the page with the values they entered still shown. Pressing Enter in an identifier field of a species panel that already has saved animals leaves every one of those animals listed in that panel's saved-animals table, and leaves every other panel's saved animals listed too. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-076, repo-frontend-p6-090, repo-frontend-p6-091; ruling:sam-2026-10-26 ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-019)

The buttons a keyboard or screen-reader user reaches inside a species panel are that panel's own save button and a 'Remove' action for each animal it has saved; tabbing forward from the panel's last identifier field reaches one of those next. increments.title: The journey tells a hard stop from a submission check, and keeps a group of answers all-or-nothing
increments.detail: The notification's data specification marks each answer as mandatory to proceed, mandatory to submit, optional or conditional, and marks some answers as a group that is filled in together. The journey's obligation model carries only mandatory or optional today, and a mandatory answer is held back to the submission check while each page's own hard stops are written into the page, so the two kinds of mandatory cannot be told apart and a half-filled group can be stored. After this row the model carries all four markings and the all-or-nothing group, and judges each one where the answer applies: on the notification, on a commodity line or on a unit. A trader is then stopped on the page only by an answer the specification makes a hard stop, is told at submission about an answer that only holds submission back, and can never store half of a group. The high-risk plants journey shares the model and takes the same change.
acceptanceCriteria: An answer the notification data specification marks mandatory to proceed must be given before its page can be left: every save control the page offers refuses a blank answer with an error naming it in the error summary and inline, the trader stays on the page with what they entered still shown, and nothing is saved. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-011, confluence-6497338582-p1-011-m1; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p2-140, repo-frontend-p2-171)

An answer the specification marks mandatory to submit can be left blank while the notification is being filled in, so every save control on its page saves and moves on with it blank, and the notification cannot be submitted until it is given, with each one still missing named when the trader tries to submit. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-012; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p2-140)

An answer the specification marks optional can be left blank throughout: its page saves and moves on without it, and the notification submits without it. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-014; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p2-171)

An answer the specification marks conditional is needed only while its stated condition holds, judged at the level the answer applies at, so the same answer can be needed for one commodity line and not for another on the same notification, and needed for one unit and not another on the same line. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-016; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p2-143)

A group of answers the specification marks all-or-nothing can be left blank as a whole, and once any answer in the group is given every save control the page offers refuses it with an error for each answer still missing from that group. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-015, confluence-6497338582-p1-011-m1; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p2-004)

The overview task row covering an all-or-nothing group reads 'Complete' when every answer in the group is given and when none of them is, and reads as still to do while only part of the group is given. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-015; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p2-160, repo-frontend-p2-159-m1)

The high-risk plants journey judges its own answers by the same four markings and the same all-or-nothing rule, with the same wording on the page and the same reading on its overview. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44)

notes: New on this re-distil, for req-2206 and req-2207, which the 2 November widening of the data specification brought in. They were given to no area, so the combiner drafted them. One row, not two: both are the same model's vocabulary, both are judged by the same evaluator and both are observed through the same pages and the same overview, so building them apart would repeat the whole set-up, review and ladder.

Its own theme, obligation-model, because the model folder (frontend:src/server/app/model/obligations and its plants twin) is the one piece of shared code no other theme touches: every feature theme changes a set's pages or its obligation sections, and the split-off themes that own shared code own the journey flow, the shared layout and the reference services.
